Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement review we need to confirm how Redwood handles transfers from the EU/UK to third countries. Specific asks from our legal team: 

- Do you rely on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for EU -> US transfers?
- For UK-resident data, will you sign the UK Addendum / IDTA (whichever Redwood uses)? We have UK-specific approval that references the IDTA, not just the SCCs.

- Do you perform TIAs/DTIAs for major subprocessors (cloud provider, logging vendors)?

We would appreciate the DPA redline and a data flow diagram for our internal DT assessment. Ideally before our legal committee meets next week (week of 11/23).

Hannah / team,

High-level legal position (summary):

1) EU transfers: we use the EU SCCs (2021 version) as our primary mechanism for controller-to-controller and processor transfers where required. For most hosted API customers we execute our DPA which incorporates the SCCs by attachment. That should satisfy EU requirements subject to any specific downstream risk issues.

2) UK coverage: the UK has its Own Addendum/IDTA regime. We offer the UK Addendum that is intended to sit alongside the SCCs (it mirrors the UK Addendum text commonly used in the market). In many cases the Addendum is accepted by UK buyers; some (conservative) customers insist on a separate standalone IDTA instead of an addendum.

Recommendation: offer SCCs + UK Addendum as the default. If the counterparty explicitly requires a standalone IDTA, escalate to Legal for a short form IDTA negotiation. The material difference is limited in practice but some customers require the separate signature flow.

3) TIAs/DTIAs: we perform internal DTIA assessments for high-risk flows and whenever a customer requests evidence. For subprocessors (GCP, logging vendor, metrics provider) we maintain vendor-specific TIAs. We can provide the TIA summary (controls and residual risk) and the full questionnaire on request under an NDA if needed.

4) Subprocessors / Switzerland: Switzerland is a separate third country. If Globe is moving Swiss-resident data, we should map Switzerland explicitly in the DF map. SCCs are commonly used; customers sometimes ask for additional safeguards for Swiss transfers — we can provide a DTIA note for those flows.

Action items (legal):
- Produce DPA redline with SCCs and include UK Addendum clause as default (Hannah / Marissa: please approve doc for sending).
- Prepare an FAQ paragraph for customers explaining when we will negotiate a standalone UK IDTA vs the Addendum.
- Confirm whether Globe requires audit evidence for any specific subprocessors (they asked generally about TIAs).

I will draft the redline language for the UK Addendum clause and attach to the DPA.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Data transfers: DPA + SCCs + UK coverage — initial questions

Quick operational checklist and evidence status:

- Subprocessor map: current export attached (DataFlow_Map_GlobeRetail.xlsx). Key subprocessors that process EEA/UK data outside the area:
  - Google Cloud (projects in us-west2, us-east4) — TIA summary available.
  - LogStream Inc (log forwarding) — processes in AWS eu-west-1 primarily, but backups in us-east-1.
  - MetricsProviderX — EU region hosted, no US ingress.

- TIAs/DTIAs: we have a TIA summary for GCP and LogStream. I attached a draft TIA responses doc (TIA_Responses_draft.pdf) that maps controls to the customer's typical questions (encryption at rest = AES-256, in transit = TLS1.2+, SOC2 Type II attestation link). Full vendor questionnaires live in /compliance/vendor/ and can be redacted for sharing.

- DPA redline: procurement (Marissa) — please see the comments Karthik suggested. I recommend we: 1) include SCCs as an annex; 2) attach the UK Addendum text as a signed addendum option; 3) include a subprocessor notice period of 14 days for new subprocessors (we already use 14 days in most SLAs).

- Swiss transfers: none of the primary processing clusters are in Switzerland, but customers may send data labelled as Swiss. We'll flag that in the DF map and include a short DTIA note explaining the safeguards (same as for other third-country flows).

Timeline estimate to assemble package for Globe: 
- Subprocessor export + TIA summary: today (attached).
- DPA redline (first pass): 1 business day if Marissa can prioritize.
- Final send to Globe with attachments + DocuSign link: by COB Monday 11/23 if legal redline approved.

Attachments included: DataFlow_Map_GlobeRetail.xlsx, TIA_Responses_draft.pdf

Soojin Lee
Privacy & Platform Ops — Redwood Inference

Sophie — thanks for the questions and patience. Attached is the package we discussed: Redwood_DPA_v2_markedup.docx (redline with SCC annex and draft UK Addendum language), DataFlow_Map_GlobeRetail.xlsx (subprocessor + flow map), and a short TIA summary for the major subprocessors (TIA_Responses_draft.pdf).

Summary / proposed path: 
1) Default approach: we will execute our standard DPA that incorporates the EU SCCs and include the UK Addendum as an accompanying signed document. This satisfies the majority of UK and EU customers.
2) If Globe's committee requires a standalone UK IDTA rather than an Addendum, please flag that explicitly and we will escalate to Legal and produce a short-form IDTA for signature (this will add ~2 business days to turnaround).
3) Subprocessor notice: we propose the standard 14-day notice for new subprocessors and will provide Globe with our current subprocessor map (attached).
4) TIAs/DTIAs: we can provide the TIA summary and SOC2 evidence. If Globe needs full vendor questionnaire responses we can share redacted versions under an NDA.

Next steps: 
- Please confirm whether the committee will accept the UK Addendum or requires a standalone IDTA.
- If accepted, we will send a DocuSign package with the DPA + SCC Annex + UK Addendum by EOD Monday 11/23. (DocuSign link will be provided: DocuSign: envelopeId=12345abcdef)
- If Globe needs additional DTIA detail for Switzerland or any other specific jurisdiction, let us know which data classes are in scope and we'll add a short jurisdictional DTIA note.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your counsel and ours if that helps speed the committee review.

Best,
